title: Rebuild your resume from a gold-standard template
detail: Start from a one-page new-grad SWE template and port your content in, cutting every line that doesn't show impact.

title: Trade resumes with a classmate for a 20-minute teardown
detail: Swap resumes, mark the weakest three bullets on each other's, and rewrite them on the spot.

title: Add a number to every bullet on your resume
detail: Go bullet by bullet and add a scale, speed-up, or user count; flag the ones you can't quantify.

title: Write down the gap your resume shows (strong projects, no internship)
detail: List what recruiters will read between the lines, then pick the one gap that is cheapest to close before applications open.

title: Ask one alum in your target role to review your resume
detail: Send a three-line message with your resume attached and one specific question about the gap you found.

title: Join one club or group in your target field
detail: Pick a club, lab, or community in the industry you're applying to and attend one meeting this month; add the role to your resume once you hold one.

title: Compete in a hackathon and ship a demo
detail: Sign up for one upcoming hackathon, scope a demo you can finish in a weekend, and put the repo and link on your resume.

title: Choose AWS as your cloud lane
detail: Largest market share and the most job postings; you'll start with IAM, EC2, S3, and Lambda.

title: Choose Azure as your cloud lane
detail: Common at enterprises and consulting firms, and tightly tied to Microsoft tooling; you'll start with resource groups, VMs, and Functions.

title: Choose GCP as your cloud lane
detail: Strong for data and ML workloads with a cleaner console; you'll start with projects, Compute Engine, and Cloud Run.

title: Work through the AWS free-tier getting-started tutorials
detail: Do three official tutorials end to end (deploy a static site, a Lambda, a container) on the free tier.

title: Work through the Azure free-account quickstarts
detail: Do three Microsoft Learn quickstarts (a web app, a Function, a container) on a free account.

title: Work through the GCP free-tier quickstarts
detail: Do three Google Cloud quickstarts (Cloud Run, a bucket, a small pipeline) on the free tier.

title: Build and deploy a small service in a hands-on sandbox
detail: Containerize a project you already have, deploy it with infrastructure-as-code and a CI pipeline, and write down what broke.

title: Take a guided cloud certification lab track
detail: A structured lab track with graded exercises toward an entry cloud certification, price [PRICE].

title: Get matched with students who share your wish
detail: Answer three questions and be introduced to two or three other seniors chasing the same industry.

title: Join a small group of five to compare notes
detail: Meet for 45 minutes with your matches to share what each of you has tried, who you've talked to, and what you'd do differently.

title: Be paired with a senior already working in the field
detail: A 30-minute monthly call with someone two to five years into the role, price [PRICE]; optional.

title: Message one alum who works in the industry you want
detail: Find one alum on LinkedIn from ASU CS, send a four-line note with one specific question, and log the reply.

title: Book three 20-minute informational chats this month
detail: Line up three people at companies you'd consider, ask each what surprised them in their first year, and write up patterns.

title: Attend one industry meetup and talk to two people
detail: Pick a meetup or career event, prepare a 30-second intro of your capstone, and follow up within 24 hours.

title: Read one seminal paper on your topic and summarize it in five bullets
detail: Pick a highly cited paper, read it in one sitting, and write five bullets: problem, idea, result, limit, what you'd try.

title: Reimplement the core idea in under 100 lines
detail: Strip the concept to its smallest working version in a notebook or script and print an intermediate value that proves it works.

title: Write a one-page explainer and give it to a friend
detail: Turn what you built into a page that a non-expert peer can follow; note where they got lost and fix it.

title: Watch the first lecture of a top university course on the topic
detail: Pick a course lecture on the topic at 1.5x speed, then write the three questions it leaves you with.

title: Turn your toughest course project into something you can demo
detail: Choose the class project you're proudest of, add a README, a demo video, and a hosted link.

title: Write a target list of 15 companies, ranked
detail: List 15 places you'd take an offer from, tag each by stage, location, and role, and rank them.

title: Do one timed mock technical interview with a peer
detail: Give each other one medium problem, 45 minutes each, and score on communication, correctness, and complexity.

title: Find your weakest problem pattern and drill it for two weeks
detail: Tag your last 20 solved problems by pattern, pick the weakest, and do two problems a day on it.

title: Request referrals at your top five companies
detail: Use your target list to find a contact at each of five, and send a short referral request with your resume.

title: Shortlist 8 grad programs and read one faculty page each
detail: For each program, note deadline, faculty match, and requirements; email no one yet.

title: Ask two professors for recommendation letters with a one-page brief
detail: Send each a brief listing your work with them, your target programs, and deadlines, at least four weeks ahead.

title: Block a weekly two-hour slot and keep it for four weeks
detail: Put a recurring block on your calendar for the wish, and log at the end of each one what moved.

title: Set up a one-page tracker for applications
detail: Make a sheet with company, stage, next action, and date; add the first ten rows today.

title: Pick an accountability partner and do a Friday check-in
detail: Agree on one metric each and send a two-line update every Friday for four weeks.

title: Automate the most repetitive part of your process
detail: Write a script or template for the step you've repeated three times, such as tailoring cover letters or logging applications.

title: Run a 30-minute retro on the last month
detail: Write what worked, what didn't, and one change to your weekly plan; commit to it in writing.

title: Cut your capstone to one demo-able slice
detail: Write the smallest end-to-end version of your capstone that you can show in a two-minute video.

title: Publish a one-page portfolio with three projects
detail: Ship a static page listing three projects with a screenshot, stack, and your specific contribution each.

title: Ship a PR that fixes one good-first-issue in a repo you already use
detail: Find an issue tagged good first issue in a tool you use, reproduce it, and open a PR with a test.

title: Build a comparison sheet for first-job decisions
detail: Score each offer or target on growth, mentorship, comp, and team, with your weights written first.

title: Draft your negotiation script for a new-grad offer
detail: Write the three asks you'd make and rehearse the call once with a friend.

title: Run a 30-minute study or working session for five peers
detail: Pick a topic you know, invite five classmates, and collect one piece of feedback afterwards.

title: Offer to mentor one underclassman for a month
detail: Set a biweekly 30-minute call with a sophomore, agree on a goal, and write down what you learned as the mentor.

title: Take the lead on a team deliverable and write the plan
detail: Volunteer to own one team deliverable, write a task breakdown with owners, and run a weekly ten-minute standup.

title: Run for an officer role or start a small recurring event
detail: Pick one group you're in, write a one-page proposal for what you'd change, and present it to the current officers.

title: Interview one engineering manager about how they got there
detail: Ask a manager what they wish they'd known at your stage and which skill mattered most; write up three takeaways.

title: Publish one technical post or thread on something you built
detail: Write about one real problem you hit in a project and how you solved it; share it in one place where engineers hang out.

title: Interview five people who have the problem you'd solve
detail: Ask what they do today and what it costs them; do not pitch. Record the exact phrases they use.

title: Ship a landing page and one working feature in a weekend
detail: Build the smallest thing that answers the first question your interviews raised and share it with three of them.

title: Get ten real users to try it and watch three of them
detail: Send it to ten people in your interview set, sit with three while they use it, and list where they stalled.

title: Find three local organizations with a problem software could fix
detail: Email or visit three nonprofits or campus groups and ask what they do manually every week.

title: Build a small pilot tool for one of them
detail: Offer to build the simplest version of the fix for one organization, and agree in writing what success looks like.

title: Write a one-page retrospective of this wish
detail: List the three moves you did, what each changed, and what you'd do first if you started over.

title: Share your path with one person who has the same wish
detail: Send your three moves to a peer and ask which one they'd swap out and why.

title: Set a three-month milestone for the wish
detail: Write one measurable outcome, the date, and the first move that gets you there.

title: Ship something public that came out of your path
detail: Pick one artifact from your moves (a post, a repo, a talk) and publish it this week.
